summary: Per Kværne is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his Mag. art. and Dr. phil. at the University of Oslo, studying under Nils Simonsson. He held posts at the University of Bergen and the University of Oslo.
Peri Sarveswara Sharma was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Wilhelm Rau from around 1966 to 1971. He held a position at the University of Marburg from approximately 1971 to 1991.

Perry Link is a sinologist and linguist who earned his B.A. from Harvard University. He taught Chinese language and literature at UCLA (1977–1988) and held professorships at Princeton University (1973–1977) and the University of California, Riverside (~2008).

Perry Schmidt-Leukel is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who completed multiple degrees, including his Habilitation, at the University of Munich. He held posts at the universities of Munich, Innsbruck, Salzburg, Glasgow, and Münster.

Peter Adamson is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Williams College and the University of Notre Dame. He held posts at King's College London from around 2000 to 2012 and at the University of Munich around 2012.
Peter Alan Roberts is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979 and under doctoral supervisor Michael Aris.

Peter C. Bisschop is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Groningen under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson. He held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford, the University of Edinburgh (2005–2010), and Leiden University.

Peter Connolly was a scholar in religious studies and Indology who completed his BA, MA, and Ph.D. at Lancaster University. In 1980, he served as a Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester.

Peter D. Hershock works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Yale University, he studied under traditional teachers Seungsahn Haengwon and Ji Kwang Dae Poep Sa Nim, and coordinated the Asian Studies Development Program at the East-West Center.
Peter Ebbatson is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Oxford under the supervision of Walpola Rahula.

Peter Fenner works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under advisers N. Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, Richard A. Hutch, and traditional teacher Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, and held a post at Deakin University.

Peter Gaeffke was an Indologist who studied at Regensburg, DIAS, and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, where he earned his PhD. He was a professor at Utrecht University (1964) and the University of Pennsylvania (1975–2003).

Peter Gyallay-Pap is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed his PhD at the London School of Economics by 1990. In 2007, he was attested as an adjunct at Adams State University.

Peter Harvey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies who founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies in 1996. He served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Sunderland.
Peter Haskel is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed graduate studies at Columbia University, where he studied under Yoshito S. Hakeda.
Peter J. Wilson earned his Ph.D. from Yale University. He taught at Yale, Vassar College, the University of Washington, Bennington College, and the University of Otago (~1971–1998).

Peter James Gilks works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed a PhD at the Australian National University under John Powers and studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang under traditional teachers including Geshe Ngawang Jangchup and Khensur Lobsang Tenpa.
Peter K. Austin is a linguist who studied at the Australian National University from 1975 to 1978. He held an academic post at SOAS University of London from approximately 2002 to 2016.

Peter Koret is a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics who completed his doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London. He has held academic posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.

Peter Kornicki is a scholar of Japanology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who earned his DPhil at Oxford and studied under Masamichi Asukai and Mitsukuni Yoshida. He held posts at Tasmania, Kyoto University, and the University of Cambridge.
